items.title: [Bug]: /v1/chat/completions drops clear_at from mid-conversation system messages on Anthropic models
items.body:
### Description

Anthropic lets a mid-conversation system message carry `clear_at` (for example `"next_user_message"`, behind the `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21` beta), so the message is hidden from the model and not billed once a later user turn or tool result arrives. On `/v1/messages` LiteLLM forwards the field. On `/v1/chat/completions` the Anthropic translation rebuilds each mid-conversation system message with only `role` and `content`, so `clear_at` never reaches Anthropic. The request still succeeds, which makes this easy to miss. The model keeps seeing every reminder the client meant to expire, and every copy is billed as input on each later request.

The client has no way around it on the chat route. Sending the beta header does not help, because the field is already gone from the body. Agents that re-send a short runtime reminder after every tool call are hit the hardest, since the stale copies pile up for the rest of the session.

I expected the chat route to keep `clear_at` on the system message it emits, the same way `/v1/messages` does. When LiteLLM merges a run of adjacent system messages into one, the merged message can only keep `clear_at` if every message in the run carries the same value, otherwise a permanent instruction would be cleared together with a turn-scoped one.

### Proposed fix

The patch below keeps `clear_at` on the system message the chat route emits, and applies the merge rule above when a run of system messages is merged. It also declares `clear_at` on the two message TypedDicts so no type suppression is needed. With it, the 3,600-token request above bills 35 prompt tokens on `/v1/chat/completions`, streaming and non-streaming, the same as `/v1/messages`. I have regression tests for it in `tests/unit/llms/anthropic/chat/test_anthropic_chat_transformation.py` and am happy to open a PR if that helps.

```diff
diff --git a/litellm/litellm_core_utils/prompt_templates/mid_conversation_system.py b/litellm/litellm_core_utils/prompt_templates/mid_conversation_system.py
index d19f290b82..7ec96d3b2b 100644
--- a/litellm/litellm_core_utils/prompt_templates/mid_conversation_system.py
+++ b/litellm/litellm_core_utils/prompt_templates/mid_conversation_system.py
@@ -192,10 +192,12 @@ def anthropic_system_messages(message: object) -> tuple[AnthropicMessagesSystemM
     blocks: Final = anthropic_system_blocks((message,))
     if not blocks:
         return ()
-    wire: Final[AnthropicMessagesSystemMessageParam] = {
-        "role": "system",
-        "content": list(blocks),
-    }
+    clear_at: Final = string_field(message, "clear_at")
+    wire: Final[AnthropicMessagesSystemMessageParam] = (
+        {"role": "system", "content": list(blocks), "clear_at": clear_at}
+        if clear_at
+        else {"role": "system", "content": list(blocks)}
+    )
     return (wire,)
 
 
@@ -217,7 +219,15 @@ def _merged_system_message(run: Sequence[object]) -> tuple[ChatCompletionSystemM
     content: Final[list[ChatCompletionTextObject]] = [  # mutable-ok: anthropic_messages_pt only recognises list content
         _openai_text_block(part) for part in parts
     ]
-    merged: Final[ChatCompletionSystemMessage] = {"role": "system", "content": content}
+    # A merged run is cleared only when every message in it carries the same clear_at, so a
+    # permanent instruction is never cleared together with a turn-scoped one.
+    clear_ats: Final = frozenset(string_field(message, "clear_at") for message in run)
+    shared_clear_at: Final = next(iter(clear_ats)) if len(clear_ats) == 1 else None
+    merged: Final[ChatCompletionSystemMessage] = (
+        {"role": "system", "content": content, "clear_at": shared_clear_at}
+        if shared_clear_at
+        else {"role": "system", "content": content}
+    )
     return (merged,)
 
 
diff --git a/litellm/types/llms/anthropic.py b/litellm/types/llms/anthropic.py
index 01ed131096..8df38bb645 100644
--- a/litellm/types/llms/anthropic.py
+++ b/litellm/types/llms/anthropic.py
@@ -432,6 +432,7 @@ class AnthropicSystemMessageContent(TypedDict, total=False):
 class AnthropicMessagesSystemMessageParam(TypedDict, total=False):
     role: Required[Literal["system"]]
     content: Required[str | Iterable[AnthropicSystemMessageContent]]
+    clear_at: str
 
 
 AllAnthropicMessageValues = AnthropicMessagesUserMessageParam | AnthopicMessagesAssistantMessageParam
diff --git a/litellm/types/llms/openai.py b/litellm/types/llms/openai.py
index 7419a417aa..c825057bfa 100644
--- a/litellm/types/llms/openai.py
+++ b/litellm/types/llms/openai.py
@@ -1028,6 +1028,7 @@ class OpenAIChatCompletionDeveloperMessage(TypedDict, total=False):
 
 class ChatCompletionSystemMessage(OpenAIChatCompletionSystemMessage, total=False):
     cache_control: ChatCompletionCachedContent
+    clear_at: str
 
 
 class ChatCompletionDeveloperMessage(OpenAIChatCompletionDeveloperMessage, total=False):
```

### Config

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: claude-opus-5-5
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

### LiteLLM Version

v1.110.2 (also reproduced on v1.105.0 and v1.109.1, and the code on main at fb7bb3143e is unchanged)

### Steps to Repro

The translation can be checked without an API key.

```python
import json, os
os.environ["LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP"] = "True"
from litellm.llms.anthropic.chat.transformation import AnthropicConfig

messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are terse."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "First question"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "First answer"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Second question"},
    {"role": "system", "content": "Reminder for this turn only.", "clear_at": "next_user_message"},
]
body = AnthropicConfig().transform_request(
    model="claude-opus-5-5", messages=messages, optional_params={}, litellm_params={}, headers={}
)
print(json.dumps([m for m in body["messages"] if m["role"] == "system"], indent=2))
```

Output on v1.110.2:

```json
[
  {
    "role": "system",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Reminder for this turn only."
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

Expected: the same message with `"clear_at": "next_user_message"`.

This is not specific to one model. On v1.110.2 the field is dropped the same way for every Claude model LiteLLM marks as supporting mid-conversation system messages, I checked claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-opus-5 and claude-opus-4-8.

Through the proxy, the effect shows up in `usage.prompt_tokens`. Put a long system message (about 3,600 tokens) between a user turn and an assistant turn, mark it with `clear_at`, and follow it with another user turn so the message should be cleared.

1. curl http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `-H "anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21"` and `{"model": "claude-opus-5-5", "max_tokens": 16, "messages": [user, {"role": "system", "content": "<~3,600 tokens>", "clear_at": "next_user_message"}, assistant, user]}`
2. Response is 200 with `usage.prompt_tokens` of 3636, the same as the identical request without `clear_at`.
3. Expected `prompt_tokens` of about 35, which is what Anthropic reports when the field reaches it (checked with the field passed through). These numbers were measured on claude-opus-5-5, and claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-haiku-5-5 gave the same counts.

### Which part of LiteLLM is this about?

LLM translation: a specific provider's request or response

### How are you deploying?

Docker

items.title: [Feature]: Per-key and per-team model ITPM/OTPM limits (provider-shaped token accounting)
items.body:
### The Feature

Allow `model_itpm_limit` / `model_otpm_limit` (same `{model_group: int}` shape as projects, #35110) on **keys and teams**, enforced by `parallel_request_limiter_v3` as separate counters alongside the existing `model_tpm_limit`, with admission-time reservation and post-call credit-back.

Observed on v1.108.10; the same gap exists on `main` (including `parallel_request_limiter_v3_native.py`).

### Motivation, pitch

Several providers enforce input and output tokens per minute **separately**, on a quota shared by every caller of a model. Databricks Foundation Model APIs is the clearest case ([limits and quotas](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/limits)):

- "Token-based rate limits … are enforced separately for input and output tokens."
- "Input tokens are counted from your actual prompt at request time."
- "If you provide `max_tokens` in your request, Databricks uses this value to estimate and reserve output token capacity before the request is admitted for processing … If `max_tokens` would cause you to exceed OTPM limits, Databricks rejects the request immediately with a 429 error."
- "if the actual token usage is less than the reserved `max_tokens`, Databricks credits the difference back to your rate limit allowance"
- "If you don't specify `max_tokens`, Databricks uses a default reservation, and the actual token count is reconciled after generation."
- "These limits are shared across all usage of that model in the workspace."

OTPM is often far below ITPM: the published defaults for several open models (e.g. GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) are 2,000,000 ITPM vs 40,000 OTPM.

Other providers account differently, so this has to be configurable per model rather than globally:

| Provider | Accounting |
|---|---|
| Databricks FMAPI | separate ITPM (actual prompt) / OTPM (reserves `max_tokens`, credits back) |
| Anthropic | separate ITPM/OTPM; "max_tokens parameter does not factor into OTPM rate limit calculations"; cache reads don't count toward ITPM ([docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/api/rate-limits)) |
| OpenAI | one TPM, "calculated as the maximum of max_tokens and the estimated number of tokens based on the character count" ([docs](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/rate-limits)) |
| Bedrock runtime | input + `max_tokens` deducted at start, settled at input + cache write + output × burndown ([docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-token-burndown.html)) |

A proxy that fronts such a quota for many keys needs a per-key OTPM limit, so that one output-heavy key can't starve everyone else. Today that isn't possible:

- Key/team per-model limits (`_add_model_per_key_rate_limit_descriptor`) are RPM plus **one** combined TPM counter.
- The token type of that counter is the **global** `general_settings.token_rate_limit_type` (`get_rate_limit_type`). Setting it to `output` to protect an OTPM-limited provider breaks the input-limited providers in the same proxy (#17480, #17664).
- Separate ITPM/OTPM exist only for:
  - **projects**: `add_project_io_token_rate_limit_descriptors_from_metadata`, which reads `project_metadata` only;
  - **deployments**: `router_utils/pre_call_checks/io_token_rate_limit_check.py`, a single counter shared by all keys.

  `model_itpm_limit` / `model_otpm_limit` are already listed in `LiteLLM_ManagementEndpoint_MetadataFields`, but the limiter never reads key or team values.
- Side issue: the combined-TPM reservation (`_estimate_tokens_for_request`) always reserves `input_estimate + output_budget`, but reconciliation uses `token_rate_limit_type`. With `output`, prompt tokens sit in an output counter until the request completes, which can cause false 429s on long-prompt requests.

### Evidence (production, anonymised)

A single key saturated a shared Databricks OTPM quota on two models for about two days. That key stayed well inside its per-key combined TPM limit, because its traffic was about 45% output tokens while the combined limit was sized for the fleet's much lower output share.

Provider 429 rate on the affected models over that period, bucketed by the request's `max_tokens`:

| `max_tokens` | 429 rate |
|---|---|
| unset | 7% |
| ≤1K | 35% |
| 1K–4K | 36% |
| 4K–16K (mostly the saturating key) | 57% |
| 16K–64K | 59% |
| >64K | 51% |

- The same synthetic probe caller on the same routes (`/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`) saw about 35% 429s with `max_tokens=2048` and **0%** with it unset. Databricks' undocumented default reservation is evidently much smaller than even a small explicit `max_tokens`.
- In the days before the saturating key started, requests with `max_tokens` close to the model's maximum were admitted with about 0% 429s. This matches the docs' "reserve `max_tokens` against what remains in OTPM".
- The provider error body we receive is `{"error_code":"REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED","message":"REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: Exceeded workspace output tokens per minute rate limit for <endpoint> …"}`. It does **not** include the `limit_type` / `retry_after` fields described in the docs.

### Proposed design

1. **Descriptors:** `model_per_key_itpm` / `model_per_key_otpm` and `model_per_team_itpm` / `model_per_team_otpm`, built from key/team metadata `model_itpm_limit` / `model_otpm_limit`.
   - Reuse the existing project path: `reserve_io_tokens` (atomic per bucket, with rollback), `_build_io_token_reservation_ops` (reconciliation), and the failure/partial-stream refund.
   - Enforce them together with `model_tpm_limit`; both apply, as they do for projects.
2. **Admission:**
   - ITPM reserves the input estimate. Prefer `token_counter` for the deployment's model, as the router check does, over chars/4.
   - OTPM reserves `explicit output cap × n`. If no cap is set, use `default_estimated_output_tokens[_per_model]` (key, then team), else `min(model max_output_tokens, otpm_limit × fraction)`, matching #49054.
   - Reject with 429 if either bucket would exceed what remains, and name the bucket in the error and in the `x-ratelimit-*` headers.
3. **Credit-back:** on success, reconcile ITPM to billable input and OTPM to completion tokens. On failure or disconnect, settle at the recovered partial usage, otherwise refund.
4. **Per-model accounting knobs**, since providers differ:
   - Whether cache reads count toward ITPM: Anthropic and Bedrock exclude them, OpenAI counts them.
   - Optionally, a per-model `model_tpm_limit_type: {model: input|output|total}` for the combined counter, as a lighter alternative to separate buckets.
   - Make the combined-TPM reservation estimate follow the token type it is reconciled against.
5. **Optional:** when a provider 429 identifies the limit, map it to `retry-after` (related: #45115). For Databricks, fall back to parsing the message text, since the documented fields aren't present in practice.
6. Parity in the native limiter (`parallel_request_limiter_v3_native.py`).

Non-goal: emulating providers' token-bucket burst buffers. A fixed 60s window is fine as long as the limits are set below the provider's.

### Related

#35110, #31952, #49054, #37001, #17480, #17664, #41957, #41395, #45115

items.title: [Bug]: model_info.default_reasoning_effort is never injected into chat request bodies — the "move it under model_info" warning overpromises
items.body:
> Filed via API (token from `openwebui/github-creds.env`) — AI-assisted drafting; all claims verified against the tagged v1.110.2 source (the deployed image) and live deployment logs.

**Description**

Setting `default_reasoning_effort` on a model gives a false sense of a working request default. Either placement behaves as follows:

- Under `litellm_params`, the router logs at startup:
  `Deployment '<model>' sets ['default_reasoning_effort'] under litellm_params, where litellm ignores them and never sends them to the provider. Move them under model_info for litellm to use them.`
  (`litellm/litellm_core_utils/routing_common_utils.py::warn_on_ignored_model_capability_flags`)
- Moving it under `model_info` silences the warning — but **the key is never injected into the outgoing request body.** `model_info.default_reasoning_effort` is parsed into the config (`litellm/utils.py` → `litellm/types/utils.py`) and consumed only by guards (`effort_resolves_to_none` in `litellm/llms/openai/chat/gpt_reasoning_transformation.py` — the temperature/top_p/sampling decision) and the codex catalog fallback (`nearest_declared_reasoning_effort`), and in error messages. The chat-completions path reads only request-level `reasoning_effort` (`_map_openai_params`, `non_default_params.get("reasoning_effort")`) — no `model_info` default is read anywhere in the request translation.

Result: a client that sends **no** `reasoning_effort` gets the provider's own default, not the configured one — silently, with no warning, no error, and no debug trace.

**Config**

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: my-model
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/my-model-backend
      api_base: http://backend:8000/v1
      api_key: os.environ/BACKEND_KEY
    model_info:
      default_reasoning_effort: "medium"   # key is accepted, silently never applied
```

**LiteLLM Version**: v1.110.2 (ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.110.2)

**Steps to Repro**

1. Start the proxy with the config above (or with `default_reasoning_effort: "medium"` under `litellm_params` — see the startup warning; then move it under `model_info` as the warning advises).
2. `curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model": "my-model", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain how a binary search tree deletes a node and rebalances."}], "max_tokens": 1024}'`
3. Actual: `200`; the backend receives no `reasoning_effort` (on a looped thinking model the provider's own default applies — `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` ~600–900, vs ~200–400 for explicit medium). Expected: the backend receives `reasoning_effort: "medium"` (or the proxy refuses the config with an actionable error, as the `models appear under litellm_params` path already does).
4. Working alternative already used: `reasoning_effort: "medium"` in `litellm_params` (our own task row) — it is forwarded (issue #8370) and takes request-explicit override; it reproduces the intended default semantics exactly.

**Notes**

- #8370 (closed) covered the original feature request — its resolution ("by setting reasoning effort in litellm_params it acts as the default already") matches the strict-pin route. This report is about the adjacent, distinct defect: the `default_reasoning_effort` key + its warning are misleading — a config-side mechanism that cannot set a request default.
- Related open PR #40240 auto-translates `thinking`/`reasoning_effort` from `model_info` — different key, different surface, does not cover `default_reasoning_effort`.

**Suggested fix**

- Inject `model_info.default_reasoning_effort` into the request when the client omits `reasoning_effort` (request-explicit wins, like a strict pin), or
- correct the warning + docs so users understand the key feeds guards only, never a request default.

items.title: [Bug]: /v1/messages input guardrails replace tool names over 64 chars with the truncated name, and it is never restored

labels.name: claude code
labels.description: Issues related to Claude Code usage

items.body:
### Description

On `/v1/messages`, a default-on input guardrail rewrites tool names longer than 64 characters to their truncated form. The model then sees and calls the truncated name, and the response carries it instead of the client's original name. So the client (Claude Code here) can't match the call to its tool.

Cause (1.108.4): `llms/anthropic/chat/guardrail_translation/handler.py` `process_input_messages`:
- It translates the request with `LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter().translate_anthropic_to_openai(...)`, which truncates long names to `{55 chars}_{8-char sha256}` (`truncate_tool_name`).
- `_translate_to_openai` drops the returned `tool_name_mapping`.
- After the guardrail runs, `guardrailed_inputs["tools"]` is converted back with `map_tool_helper` and written to `data["tools"]` with the truncated names. Nothing restores them, in the request or on the response path.

Without the guardrail, the same request works: called through the SDK (`litellm.anthropic.messages.acreate`), the response carries the original name, for both a Bedrock Anthropic model and a Bedrock Converse model.

### Config

```yaml
guardrails:
  - guardrail_name: secrets
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: litellm_content_filter
      mode: [pre_call]
      default_on: true
      patterns:
        - pattern_type: regex
          name: aws_access_key
          pattern: '\b(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16})\b'
          action: MASK
```

### LiteLLM Version

1.108.4

### Steps to Repro

`POST /v1/messages` through the proxy with the guardrail above, any Bedrock model (seen with `bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-haiku-*` and `bedrock/converse/qwen.qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-v1:0`), streaming or not:

```json
{"model": "<model>", "max_tokens": 100, "tool_choice": {"type": "any"},
 "tools": [{"name": "mcp__websearch-release-notes-writer__websearch-web-search-tool___WebSearch",
            "description": "web search",
            "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["query"]}}],
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "search the go version"}]}
```

- Response `tool_use.name`: `mcp__websearch-release-notes-writer__websearch-web-sear_0be153cd`.
- Expected: `mcp__websearch-release-notes-writer__websearch-web-search-tool___WebSearch` (what the SDK path returns).

Possible fix: keep the adapter's `tool_name_mapping` in `process_input_messages`, and map the guardrailed tools back to their original names before writing `data["tools"]`.

### Which part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy, guardrails, `/v1/messages`

items.title: [Bug]: Responses image_generation tool with output_format=svg: svg_usage (the SVG author model's tokens) is never billed
items.body:
### What happened

A `/v1/responses` request whose `image_generation` tool sets `output_format: "svg"` and `svg: {"model": "<chat model>"}` makes OpenAI run that second model to write the SVG. OpenAI reports its tokens in `svg_usage` on the `image_generation_call` output item, separately from `tool_usage.image_gen`:

```json
{"type": "image_generation_call", "status": "completed", "output_format": "svg",
 "svg_usage": {"input_tokens": 2235, "model": "gpt-6-luna", "output_tokens": 332,
               "reasoning_tokens": 257, "total_tokens": 2567}}
```

`completion_cost(call_type="aresponses")` bills the response's `usage` and the tool's image, but never reads `svg_usage`, so the author model's tokens are free. This happens non-streamed, streamed (`response.completed` carries the same item) and over the Responses WebSocket. It is the Responses-path sibling of #53749 / #52571, which cover `svg_usage` on `/v1/images/generations` only. Still the case on `main` (`StandardBuiltInToolCostTracking._handle_image_generation_cost` has no `svg_usage` handling).

### Version

litellm 1.108.10

### Root cause

`litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/tool_call_cost_tracking.py`, `_handle_image_generation_cost`: it prices `image_generation_call` items from `tool_usage.image_gen` with `tools[].model` only. Nothing on the Responses cost path reads an output item's `svg_usage` or the tool's `svg.model`.

### Expected

Each reported `svg_usage` is added to the cost at the author model's rates (OpenAI reports `reasoning_tokens` inside `output_tokens` when `total_tokens == input_tokens + output_tokens`).

### Repro

No network or credentials needed. `pip install 'litellm[proxy]==1.108.10' pytest; pytest -q this_file.py` gives 1 failure and 1 passing control.

```python
"""Repro: a Responses image_generation tool's svg_usage is never billed.

pip install 'litellm[proxy]==1.108.10' pytest; pytest -q this_file.

No credentials or network are needed. A Responses request whose image_generation tool
asks for output_format=svg has OpenAI run a second model, tools[].svg.model, to write
the SVG, and report that model's tokens in the image_generation_call item's svg_usage.
completion_cost on clean 1.108.10 bills the response's own usage and the tool's image,
but never svg_usage, so the author model's tokens are free. Clean 1.108.10 has 1 failure
and 1 passing control; both pass with the fix applied.

"""

import os

os.environ.setdefault("LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP", "True")

import litellm  # noqa: E402
import pytest  # noqa: E402
from litellm.types.llms.openai import ResponsesAPIResponse  # noqa: E402

AUTHOR_RATES = {
    "litellm_provider": "openai",
    "mode": "chat",
    "input_cost_per_token": 1e-7,
    "output_cost_per_token": 5e-7,
}
# As OpenAI returned it on 2026-11-23; total_tokens shows reasoning inside output_tokens.
SVG_USAGE = {
    "input_tokens": 2235,
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "output_tokens": 332,
    "reasoning_tokens": 257,
    "total_tokens": 2567,
}


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def author_prices():
    added = [
        name
        for name in ("gpt-6-luna", "openai/gpt-6-luna")
        if name not in litellm.model_cost
    ]
    for name in added:
        litellm.model_cost[name] = AUTHOR_RATES
    litellm.get_model_info.cache_clear()
    yield
    for name in added:
        del litellm.model_cost[name]
    litellm.get_model_info.cache_clear()


def svg_tool_response(svg_usage: dict | None) -> ResponsesAPIResponse:
    image_call = {
        "type": "image_generation_call",
        "id": "ig_1",
        "status": "completed",
        "output_format": "svg",
        "result": "PHN2Zy8+",
    }
    if svg_usage is not None:
        image_call["svg_usage"] = svg_usage
    return ResponsesAPIResponse.model_validate(
        {
            "id": "resp_svg",
            "object": "response",
            "created_at": 0,
            "status": "completed",
            "model": "gpt-5-nano",
            "output": [image_call],
            "tools": [
                {
                    "type": "image_generation",
                    "model": "gpt-image-1",
                    "output_format": "svg",
                    "svg": {"model": "gpt-6-luna"},
                },
            ],
            "usage": {
                "input_tokens": 3608,
                "output_tokens": 2341,
                "total_tokens": 5949,
            },
        },
    )


def responses_cost(response: ResponsesAPIResponse) -> float:
    return litellm.completion_cost(
        completion_response=response,
        model="gpt-5-nano",
```
